title: Explainable Batching & Caching Guardrails Panel with Rollout Preview
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal:
Design an interactive Console panel that surfaces Redwood's automated batching and KV-caching recommendations, explains the rationale, simulates cost/latency impact, and provides safe rollout controls (canary, percent-based, automatic rollback on SLO regressions). The panel should be explainable to engineers and PMs, auditable for security/compliance teams, and operable without deep infra knowledge.

Why this ticket exists:
- Customers are reluctant to enable aggressive batching/quantization without understanding risk to latency and quality.
- PMs want a single UI to apply recommendations per-route or globally and to preview financial impact before committing.
- Platform/infra needs telemetry hooks and explicit consent paths for automatic rollouts and guardrail enforcement.

Primary user stories:
- As an engineer, I want a per-route recommendation card that shows why a batching/caching suggestion was made (traffic patterns, median sequence length, token churn), so I can trust it.
- As a PM, I want to preview projected monthly cost delta and expected p95 latency change if applied cluster-wide.
- As a platform operator, I want to schedule a staged rollout with automatic rollback triggers when latency SLO or error rate thresholds are crossed.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want an audit trail that records which recommendation was accepted, who approved it, and the metrics during the canary.

Key panels and components (proposed):
- Recommendation Inspector (left column): small cards per route/model with: current config snapshot, recommended change (batch size, KV-cache TTL, skip-prefix heuristics), confidence score (high/med/low), one-line rationale. Tapping expands details.
- Explainability View (center): time-series overlays showing historical latency, token distribution, cache hit-rate, and a simulated delta projection for 1h/24h/30d. Hover reveals token-level examples where caching changed model inputs/outputs.
- Safety & Rollout Composer (right): selectors for scope (route / service / global), canary percentage slider, rollout cadence (instant / 5m / 1h), automated rollback checkboxes (p95 latency, error-rate, hallucination metric). "Preview rollout" opens a timeline with estimated impact and expected fallbacks.
- Cost Impact Preview (banner): deterministic estimate of monthly savings with sensitivity (low/median/high) and currency conversion. Links to route-level token counts.
- Audit & Rationale Panel (modal): stores the generated explanation text, recommended commit diff, and links to underlying telemetry (Grafana / traces). Includes "Add approver" flow and required sign-off toggles for enterprise customers.

Accessibility & copy guidance:
- Use concise, non-jargon labels ("Batch size" rather than "microbatch cap"). Provide inline tooltips and an optional guided tour. Ensure all interactive elements keyboard-focusable, aria labels for charts, and color choices meet AA contrast.

Telemetry and backend contract (design notes for eng):
- Each recommendation card must be tied to a recommendation_id returned by backend, include: baseline_metrics, delta_estimates, confidence_score_reason tokens, and preview_snapshot. UI will call /recommendations/preview and /recommendations/apply endpoints.
- Add telemetry events: rec_preview_shown, rec_applied, rec_rolled_back, rec_approved. Include user_id, route_id, applied_config, and canary_percentage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype with interactive frames for Inspector, Explainability, and Rollout Composer shared with PM/Eng.
- Usability test (n=6 engineers/PMs) showing >80% success on: "interpret recommendation", "create a 10% canary rollout", "find cost savings estimate".
- Design handoff docs listing required backend fields and telemetry events.
- Accessibility checklist completed and reviewed.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Automatic model-level quantization workflows and kernel selection UIs (separate infra work).
- Live edit of runtime batching algorithms; this ticket surfaces config only and relies on backend to enforce safe changes.

Notes on uniqueness vs earlier work:
- This design emphasizes explainability/traces and an auditable approval flow rather than onboarding wizards or broad recommendation hubs. The core difference: token-level explainability + rollout simulation timeline + compliance-ready audit modal.
comments: 2025-11-06 - Initial sketch uploaded to Figma (link below). Quick sync with Eng (Liam) — backend needs a recommendation_id and preview endpoint. Action: eng to propose API by 2025-11-10.
2025-11-08 - PM review (Diego) requested clearer labels for "confidence" and asked for a low/med/high translation and a raw score. Updated copy to include both.
2025-11-10 - Design crit: flagged complexity in Explainability hover state. Decided to ship a simplified token example with an expand action for full traces (to reduce initial dev cost).
2025-11-11 - Security note from Compliance (Anika): audit trail must include approver email and tenant id; added Audit & Rationale modal requirement.
2025-11-12 - Engineering review (Liam): agreed on endpoints and telemetry; asked us to include explicit rollback thresholds in the UI (added). PM approved prototype for usability sessions.
review_feedback: Simplify the Explainability hover content — engineering prefers an expandable example rather than full trace by default.
Make confidence both human-readable and numeric. Include a short "why we recommend this" sentence pulled from model heuristics.
Add explicit required sign-off when applying changes globally for enterprise orgs.
Show a pre-apply dry-run that lists exact configuration diffs and the affected routes.
decisions: Ship Inspector + Explainability + Rollout Composer as a single console page; defer global scheduling automation to next cycle.
Expose canary as percent slider (0-100) with preflight validation for small fleets to avoid sub-1% ambiguous rollouts.
Include audit modal and store recommendation_id for traceability.
